[element-name]
=== `<name>` Name of Person (Structured)

Container element for the component elements of personal names, such as a <<element-surname,`<surname>`>>.

#### Usage/Remarks
The STS model for `<name>` is a series of elements in a particular order with no punctuation or spacing between elements. For situations where a different element order is desired or punctuation between name parts is wanted, use the <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>>, which is a very loose element, which may contain text, numbers, special characters, generated text, and any or all of the naming elements, such as <<element-surname,`<surname>`>>.
##### Best Practice

If the name parts are unknown or untagged, the whole name can be placed: Within the <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>> element in contexts where <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>> is allowed, for example, “`<string-name>Ice Cube</string-name>`”; or Within the element <<element-surname,`<surname>`>> in contexts where only <<element-name,`<name>`>> is allowed, for example, “`<surname>Ice Cube</surname>`”. Use of a <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>> or <<element-surname,`<surname>`>> element is more likely to lead to better search results than merely leaving the person’s name untagged.

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-contrib,`<contrib>`>>, <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, <<element-name-alternatives,`<name-alternatives>`>>, <<element-person-group,`<person-group>`>>, <<element-related-article,`<related-article>`>>, <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>
#### Description

The following, in order: Any one of: The following, in order: <<element-surname,`<surname>`>> <<element-surname,Surname>> <<element-given-names,`<given-names>`>> <<element-given-names,Given (First) Names>>, zero or one <<element-given-names,`<given-names>`>> <<element-given-names,Given (First) Names>> <<element-prefix,`<prefix>`>> <<element-prefix,Prefix (in a name)>>, zero or one <<element-suffix,`<suffix>`>> <<element-suffix,Suffix (in a name)>>, zero or one
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  name         ( ( (surname, given-names?) | given-names),
                          prefix?, suffix?)                          >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(((surname, given-names?) | given-names), prefix?, suffix?)
